status: source-traced with frame-snapshot corroboration; exact character visibility edge still has a possible one-frame offset

text_speed.rom_effect: F2 reads its next byte into RAM $55. For each $00-$D7 text byte, the interpreter calls glyph helper $88CA, increments the text X cursor, then calls $895D if $55 is nonzero before advancing the script pointer.
text_speed.measured_model: Observed source-pointer spacing equals the active $55 operand: one next text byte per 1 source frame at speed 1; one per 5 source frames at speed 5.

ppu_sample.interpretation: One glyph update is observed per speed interval in these samples. With PPUCTRL $2000=$84, each PPUDATA write increments PPUADDR by 32: the zero write and glyph value are vertically separated by 32 address bytes. Frame-end RAM pointer samples and cycle-stamped PPU writes are different observation times; do not use one as an exact sub-frame timestamp. These register writes alone do not prove final raster-visible screen coordinates.

fc_dialog_line_block.confirmed_handler_behavior: On the captured cold-start path, the bank-0 dispatch table stores $8836 for FC as an RTS return address. RTS enters at $8837; the live trace then returns to the main interpreter and dispatches the next script byte at pointer $A055. FC does not consume a count or following payload in this observed context.
fc_dialog_line_block.not_resolved: The complete visual effects of the $8837 handler, other FC contexts, all command boundaries and the exact raster-visible schedule are unresolved. The independent PPU writes below are not attributed to FC.

independent_ppu_samples.interpretation: Observed PPU register writes only; their producer, script-byte ownership and raster-visible coordinates are not proven.

fc_dialog_line_block.integration: Keep the VM isolated until all dispatches, pointer changes, handler side effects and timing are traced on the cold-start path.

observed_ram_pointer_boundaries.command: ED $58 has queued; DC pause follows

cold_start_edges.interpretation: The DF pointer span is 240 frame intervals, A028 at frame 27 to A029 at 267. EA's screen-off/clear work occupies about 15 observed frame states before the sound command is queued. RAM snapshots are end-of-frame, so event-visible edge may be offset by one frame.
